question: What is the vault of the baby's skull made of?
explanation: Think of the baby's skull vault like puzzle pieces that aren't glued together yet! This clever design lets the head gently change shape so the baby can pass safely through the birth canal. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h1)

question: Which landmark sits right between the front and back fontanelles on a baby's head?
explanation: You've got this! The vertex is simply the top part of the head, located right between the two main soft spots (fontanelles). [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h1)

question: What shape is the anterior fontanelle (the front soft spot) of a newborn?
explanation: The front soft spot (anterior fontanelle) is nicely diamond-shaped. This is a classic midwifery detail that helps you tell it apart from the triangular back soft spot! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h2)

question: Why are the spaces (sutures) between the baby's skull bones so important during labour?

options.A: They lock the head in a fixed position to stop accidental rotation.
options.B: They supply oxygen directly to the developing foetal brain tissue.
options.C: They prevent any fluid from entering the cranial vault during birth.
options.D: They allow the skull bones to overlap and reduce the head size.

explanation: Those little gaps act like expansion joints! They let the skull bones slide over each other slightly, making the head a bit smaller so it can fit smoothly through the pelvis. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h2)

question: When a baby's head is nicely tucked with the chin to the chest, what is the measurement of the suboccipito-bregmatic diameter?
explanation: When the baby tucks its chin right into its chest, it presents its smallest and best measurement for birth: 9.5 centimeters. Beautiful design by nature! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h3)

question: If a baby's head enters the pelvis leading with the longest chin-to-forehead (mentoventricular) measurement, what is the likely outcome?

options.A: Labour will proceed rapidly because this is the smallest skull measurement.
options.B: The baby is in an ideal position for a normal spontaneous delivery.
options.C: The head will easily mould to fit through the pelvic outlet without issues.
options.D: Vaginal birth is extremely difficult or impossible due to the large size.

explanation: At 14 centimeters, this is the biggest measurement of the head. It's too wide to easily fit through, which usually makes a normal vaginal delivery very difficult. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h3)

question: What is the standard measurement of the biparietal diameter (BPD) in a full-term baby?
explanation: The biparietal diameter—the distance from one side of the head to the other—is roughly 9.5 centimeters at full term. You'll see this number all the time on ultrasound scans! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h4)

question: Which of these side-to-side measurements is the wider one across a baby's skull?
explanation: The biparietal diameter stretches across the widest part of the parietal bones, making it broader than the bitemporal measurement across the temples. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h4)

question: In midwifery, what does the term 'foetal attitude' actually mean?

options.A: The rate of cervical dilation over a specific time period
options.B: The position of the placenta inside the lower uterine segment
options.C: The relationship of foetal body parts to one another
options.D: The emotional mood of the mother during contractions

explanation: Don't let the word 'attitude' confuse you—it simply describes how the baby's head and limbs are curled up against its trunk (usually tucked in nicely like a little ball). [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h5)

question: Which neck position makes the submento-bregmatic diameter present itself to the birth canal?
explanation: When the baby's neck is stretched all the way back (complete extension, like in a face presentation), it presents the submento-bregmatic diameter instead of the usual top of the head. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h5)

question: What is the main job of 'moulding' during labour?

options.A: To increase the total volume of brain tissue
options.B: To permanently fuse the cranial sutures early
options.C: To prevent the baby from breathing amniotic fluid
options.D: To reduce the skull dimensions to fit the pelvis

explanation: Moulding is the baby's superpower for birth! The skull bones gently overlap so the head shapes itself to fit easily through the birth canal without harming the brain. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h6)

question: During a vaginal examination, a midwife notices the baby's skull bones are overlapping tightly and cannot be pushed apart with a finger. How is this graded?
explanation: When the bones overlap strongly and won't budge under finger pressure, we call that Grade 3 moulding. It's an important sign that tells us to watch out for tight squeezes (cephalopelvic disproportion)! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h6)
